the cephalospornins possess an equal or greater in vitro activity against B. gingivalis and/or B. intermedius than traditional tetraciclins and metronidazole, and a greater activity than ampicillin and piperacillin.
cephalosporine antibiotics are effective against Bacteroides species.
cephalosporines have an equal or greater in vitro inhibitory activity than traditional tetraciclins and other antibiotics, against B. gingivalis and against B. intermedius.

the in vitro sensitivity to different classes of chemioantibiotics, including two cephalosprins, of two species of anaerobic bacteria, Bacteroides (B.) gingivalis and (B.) intermedius, which are frequently isolated from periodontal pockets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the in vitro sensitivity pattern of the bacteria studied was as follows: metronidazole > tetracyclins > cephalosporines > piperacillins.
the cephalo-sporins, especially cefuroxime, are the most effective antibiotics in vitro against B. gingivalis and, in general, against B. intermedius.

, for the treatment of severe forms of periodontal disease with an aggressive and rapid onset, the antibiotic regimen to be used should include metronidazole, cefotaxim and cefuroxime, and possibly also ampicillin and piperacillin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cephalospornins, which have been used for a long time in other fields of medicine, may be considered as an alternative in periodontal therapy.
the cephalospornins have an excellent in vitro activity against the two bacteria studied, but that further in vivo studies are required.
the in vitro sensitivity tests of Bacteroidaceae to different antibiotics are useful in the selection of an effective antibiotic therapy for periodontal diseases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cephalospornin class of drugs is a good candidate for the treatment of periodontal diseases.
Bacteroides species can be inhibited in vitro by cephalosporinic compounds.
B. gingivalis and the other species of Bacteroidaceae are highly sensitive to antibiotics of the beta-lactam family, including the cephalosprins.
